findings.title: Unvalidated exception handlers may allow execution of attacker-controlled code
findings.explanation: The constructor now accepts a Mapping of arbitrary keys to ExceptionHandler callables without validation. If an attacker can supply a handler, they could execute malicious code when an exception occurs.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate or restrict the supplied handlers to trusted callables, or document that handlers must be from trusted sources.
findings.verdict_reason: The middleware now accepts an arbitrary mapping of exception handlers and adds them without validating the handler callables, allowing attacker-controlled code to be executed when an exception occurs.

findings.title: Catch-all handlers raise NotImplementedError instead of returning a response
findings.explanation: The newly added async_catch_all_handler and sync_catch_all_handler are registered to handle any Exception, but they raise NotImplementedError rather than returning a JSONResponse. When an exception occurs, the middleware will invoke these handlers, resulting in another exception and a 500 error instead of the intended custom handling.
